definition: Social feedback is the support, criticism, attention, or other responses people receive from others, especially through social networks or social media. Because it can spread through large linked networks, it can quickly reach many people and strongly affect emotions, decisions, and everyday outcomes.

reasons: The definition adds unsupported content such as “attention” and “everyday outcomes”; the packet supports support/criticism and effects on emotions, careers, and lives, but not that broader wording.

“Decisions” is only supported in the general phrase “social feedback is fundamental to human interactions and decision-making,” not as a specific downstream effect of rapid networked feedback as the definition states.

The packet supports social feedback in social-media/network contexts, but the definition should stay within the packet’s narrower description rather than generalizing to all responses people receive from others.
The packet does not explicitly support the inclusion of “attention” as one of the components of social feedback (it describes support and criticism, but not attention as such).

The packet supports effects on emotions and on decision-making, but it does not explicitly support the phrase “everyday outcomes” as written in the definition (it mentions effects on emotions, careers, and lives).
